title: UVM: Virtual Sequence
constraints: Write `class top_vseq extends uvm_sequence` (no item type) with public handles `uvm_sequencer #(cfg_item) cfg_sqr` and `uvm_sequencer #(data_item) data_sqr`. The test sets them and starts the sequence on `null`.

`body()`: (1) write register 0x00 = 0x01, then 0x04 = 0x08 on the config agent. (2) **In parallel**: a `data_burst_seq` with `n = 8` on the data agent, and a write of 0x08 = 0xAB on the config agent. (3) When both finish, write 0x00 = 0x00.
Use the provided `cfg_write_seq` and `data_burst_seq`, started on the right sequencers. The hidden drivers log when each item completes.
hints: A virtual sequence doesn't generate items itself: it starts sub-sequences on other sequencers: `s.start(cfg_sqr, this)`.
Use `fork … join` for step 2, so that step 3 waits for both branches.
Passing `this` as the parent sequence keeps the sequence hierarchy (and priorities / responses) intact.

examples.title: ordering
examples.expected: writes 0x00, 0x04 finish before any data item

examples.title: parallel
examples.expected: the 0x08 write completes during the burst
